executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) and PAHO (November 2025-April 2026) reveals a multi-threat landscape across Europe and the Americas. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, is flagged across two separate PAHO updates (November 2025 and March 2026), indicating sustained zoonotic spillover risk in the Americas region. Additional elevated concerns include mpox, yellow fever, dengue, and measles circulating concurrently in the Americas, while Europe monitors communicable disease threats across five consecutive weekly reports. Respiratory virus co-circulation—including seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis—presents compounding public health burden heading into the 2026 Southern Hemisphere influenza season.
bottomLine: Sustained H5N1 zoonotic activity in the Americas combined with concurrent outbreaks of mpox, yellow fever, dengue, and measles signals a high-complexity, multi-pathogen threat environment requiring coordinated regional response.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Two separate PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026) indicating sustained H5N1 activity
BSL-3 select agent with documented zoonotic spillover to humans
Ongoing animal-to-human transmission risk across the Americas region
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance protocols; coordinate with veterinary and agricultural authorities; ensure antiviral stockpile readiness and PPE availability for exposed workers

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23 2026 indicating active transmission
Ongoing circulation in the Americas with potential for cross-border spread
Previous global emergency precedent elevates monitoring priority
threats.action: Strengthen contact tracing and case detection; ensure vaccine availability for high-risk populations; coordinate cross-border surveillance data sharing

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13 2026 indicating active risk
Endemic amplification in sylvatic cycle with human spillover potential
Vector (Aedes/Haemagogus) activity in affected regions
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers; enhance entomological surveillance; investigate sylvatic case clusters

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 18 2026 indicating elevated case counts
Historical hyperendemicity across the Americas amplifying 2026 risk
Concurrent Chikungunya alert suggests shared Aedes aegypti vector pressure
threats.action: Intensify vector control interventions; enhance hospital surge capacity; implement case-based surveillance to detect serotype shifts

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 10 2026
Co-circulation with dengue via shared Aedes aegypti vector increases diagnostic complexity
Potential for geographic expansion into previously unaffected areas
threats.action: Integrate chikungunya diagnostics into dengue surveillance platforms; implement combined vector control strategies; monitor for unusual geographic spread

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3 2026
Post-pandemic vaccination coverage gaps creating susceptible cohorts
Risk of resurgence in communities with suboptimal MMR coverage
threats.action: Conduct rapid vaccination coverage assessments; implement catch-up immunization campaigns; strengthen case-based surveillance and outbreak response protocols

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO updates (December 2025 and March 2026) indicating sustained elevated activity
Waning immunity in adolescents and adults creating transmission reservoirs
Infants under one year at highest risk of severe disease and mortality
threats.action: Promote maternal Tdap vaccination and infant immunization schedules; investigate potential circulation of macrolide-resistant strains; strengthen laboratory diagnostic capacity

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 19 2025
Case fatality rates of 30-40% in confirmed pulmonary syndrome cases
Rodent population dynamics and human encroachment driving periodic surges
threats.action: Enhance rodent exposure risk communication; strengthen healthcare provider recognition and early supportive care protocols; improve environmental surveillance in high-risk areas

selectAgentSummary: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) — a BSL-3 select agent — was flagged in two PAHO epidemiological updates covering the Americas region (November 24 2025 and March 11 2026), indicating persistent zoonotic activity over a multi-month period. No BSL-4 pathogens were identified in the current report set. H5N1 detections are assessed as Critical threat level given the agent classification, documented human spillover potential, and sustained regional activity requiring heightened biosafety and public health response measures.

diseases: Multiple communicable disease threats (ECDC Weekly Reports)

amrSignals: Potential macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis circulation suggested by sustained transmission despite treatment — two consecutive PAHO updates over 3-month period warrant strain characterization
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (February 2026) may complicate clinical presentations and differential diagnosis in metabolic and infectious disease co-morbidity settings
emergingPatterns: Concurrent multi-pathogen respiratory burden: seasonal influenza, RSV, and pertussis co-circulating in the Americas during 2025-2026 transition period
Southern Hemisphere 2026 influenza season commencing (PAHO April 27 2026) with potential for novel strain emergence
Vector-borne disease convergence: simultaneous dengue and chikungunya alerts indicate intensified Aedes aegypti transmission pressure across the Americas
H5N1 sustained zoonotic activity across two surveillance periods (November 2025 to March 2026) suggests endemic amplification rather than isolated spillover events
Vaccine-preventable disease resurgence (measles, pertussis) indicating pandemic-era immunization gaps not yet fully recovered
